ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the radius of sector $OAB$ is $6$, $C$ is any point on arc $AB$ (not coinciding with $A$ or $B$), $CM\perp OA$ with the foot of the perpendicular being $M$, $CN\perp OB$ with the foot of the perpendicular being $N$, connecting $MN$. If $\angle AOB=45^\circ$, what is the length of $MN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect OC, extend OA and NC to intersect at D, then OC = 6, \\
$\because$ CM $\perp$ OA, CN $\perp$ OB, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DMC = $\angle$DNO = $90^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $\angle$D = $\angle$D, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$DMC $\sim$ $\triangle$DNO, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{DM}{DN}=\frac{DC}{DO}$, which implies $\frac{DM}{DC}=\frac{DN}{DO}$, \\
$\because$ $\angle$D = $\angle$D, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$DMN $\sim$ $\triangle$DCO, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{MN}{CO}=\frac{DN}{DO}$, \\
$\because$ CN $\perp$ OB, $\angle$AOB = $45^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ sin$\angle$AOB = $\frac{DN}{OD}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{MN}{OC}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, \\
$\because$ OC = 6, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{MN}{6}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, \\
$\therefore$ MN = $\boxed{3\sqrt{2}}$.

method.method_draft: Use an auxiliary circle. First read from the diagram that OA and OB are the two sides of the sector with vertex O, C lies on the arc AB, and the perpendiculars from C meet OA and OB at M and N, with MN drawn. From the text, OC is a radius of the sector, so OC = 6, and angle AOB = 45°. Since M lies on OA and CM ⟂ OA, angle OMC = 90°; since N lies on OB and CN ⟂ OB, angle ONC = 90°. The chord MN is subtended by the inscribed angle MON, so MN = OC · sin(45°) = 6 · √2/2 = 3√2.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates and orthogonal projections. Read from the diagram that M and N are the perpendicular projections of C onto the two rays OA and OB. From the text, take OC = 6 and angle AOB = 45°. Set O = (0,0), let OA be the positive x-axis, and let OB make angle θ = 45° with OA. Write C = 6(cos t, sin t), where 0 < t < θ. Then M, the projection of C onto OA, is M = (6 cos t, 0). Let u = (cos θ, sin θ) be the unit vector along OB; then N = (C · u)u = 6 cos(t - θ)(cos θ, sin θ). Compute MN² = |6 cos t(1,0) - 6 cos(t - θ)u|² = 36[cos²t + cos²(t - θ) - 2 cos θ cos t cos(t - θ)]. The trigonometric identity simplifies the bracket to sin²θ, so MN = 6 sin θ = 6 sin45° = 3√2.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：附图中，点 O 在左侧，射线 OA 向右上方，射线 OB 向右下方，弧 AB 位于右侧形成扇形边界；点 C 位于弧 AB 上；从 C 向 OA 作垂线，垂足标为 M；从 C 向 OB 作垂线，垂足标为 N；图中连接了 MN。

推理：按坐标投影法，设 O=(0,0)，令 OA 为 x 轴正方向，OB 与 OA 的夹角为 θ=45°。因为 C 在半径为 6 的弧 AB 上，所以 OC=6。设 C=6(cos t, sin t)，其中 0<t<θ。

M 是 C 到 OA 的正交投影，所以 M=(6cos t,0)。设 OB 方向的单位向量为 u=(cos θ, sin θ)，则 N 是 C 到 OB 的正交投影，因此 N=(C·u)u=6cos(t−θ)(cos θ, sin θ)。

于是 MN²=|M−N|²=|6cos t(1,0)−6cos(t−θ)u|²=36[cos²t+cos²(t−θ)−2cosθ cos t cos(t−θ)]。

利用恒等式可化简括号为 sin²θ，因此 MN=6sinθ。代入 θ=45°，得 MN=6sin45°=6·√2/2=3√2。

于是 MN²=|M−N|²=|6cos t(1,0)−6cos(t−θ)u|²=36[cos²t+cos²(t−θ)−2cosθ cos t cos(t−θ)]。

利用恒等式可化简括号为 sin²θ，因此 MN=6sinθ。代入 θ=45°，得 MN=6sin45°=6·√2/2=3√2。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, it is known that the radius of sector $OAB$ is $6$, $C$ is any point on arc $AB$ (not coinciding with $A$ or $B$), $CM\perp OA$ with the foot of the perpendicular being $M$, $CN\perp OB$ with the foot of the perpendicular being $N$, connecting $MN$. If $\angle AOB=45^\circ$, what is the length of $MN$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect OC, extend OA and NC to intersect at D, then OC = 6, \\
$\because$ CM $\perp$ OA, CN $\perp$ OB, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DMC = $\angle$DNO = $90^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $\angle$D = $\angle$D, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$DMC $\sim$ $\triangle$DNO, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{DM}{DN}=\frac{DC}{DO}$, which implies $\frac{DM}{DC}=\frac{DN}{DO}$, \\
$\because$ $\angle$D = $\angle$D, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$DMN $\sim$ $\triangle$DCO, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{MN}{CO}=\frac{DN}{DO}$, \\
$\because$ CN $\perp$ OB, $\angle$AOB = $45^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ sin$\angle$AOB = $\frac{DN}{OD}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{MN}{OC}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, \\
$\because$ OC = 6, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{MN}{6}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, \\
$\therefore$ MN = $\boxed{3\sqrt{2}}$

Point C is located on arc AB, and does not coincide with A or B. From C, perpendiculars are drawn respectively to OA and OB, with feet M and N; MN is also connected in the figure.
Reasoning: According to the problem statement, OC is the radius of the sector, so OC = 6. Because M is on OA and CM ⟂ OA, ∠OMC = 90°; because N is on OB and CN ⟂ OB, ∠ONC = 90°. Therefore M and N are both on the auxiliary circle with OC as diameter. The diameter of this circle is OC = 6, so the radius is 3. Also because OM is along OA and ON is along OB, ∠MON = ∠AOB = 45°. In this auxiliary circle, ∠MON is an inscribed angle, and the corresponding chord is MN, therefore MN = OC · sin45° = 6 · √2/2 = 3√2.
